title: Test suite wall clock is link time, not test time: 184 test binaries, default linker
description:
Mark noticed 2026-11-22: "this is a long test suite." Measured it rather
than guessed.

THE NUMBERS, from a full `cargo test --workspace --all-features` run:
- 210 test targets, all passing.
- Total time INSIDE the tests: about 336 seconds, by summing every
  "finished in Ns" line. The slowest single target was 43s; everything
  else was under 15s.
- Wall clock: roughly 25 minutes.

So about four fifths of the wall clock is not running tests. It is
compiling and linking.

THE CAUSE: 184 integration test files across the workspace, each of
which cargo builds as its own binary, each statically linking the whole
dependency graph (openmls, axum, sqlx, tokio, hickory). Per crate:

    mimid-server      61
    mimi-mls          27
    mimid-agent       18
    mimi-protocol     16
    mimi-room-policy  16
    mimid-agent-core  13
    mimid-agent-jmap  11
    mimi-content       9
    mimid-agent-store  7
    mimid-live         3
    mls-didwebvh       3

And `.cargo/config.toml` sets no linker, so this is 184 links with the
default bfd linker.

WHAT NOT TO DO: merging the test files. One file per concern is why the
tests are readable and why a bead's regression test is easy to find, and
AGENTS.md's one-subagent-per-bead workflow depends on agents not editing
the same file. The file count is a feature.

WHAT TO TRY, cheapest first:
1. A faster linker. `mold` (apt candidate 2.30.0) or `lld` (18.0),
   selected in .cargo/config.toml. Link-bound builds typically improve
   several-fold, no code or test changes, and it is one file. Neither is
   installed on the dev box yet; gold is, and is better than bfd but
   well behind mold.
2. Measure before and after on a clean target dir, so the claim is a
   measurement rather than folklore. Also check CI, where the win may be
   larger or smaller depending on the runner.
3. cargo-nextest would parallelise the RUNNING, which is only the 336
   seconds, so expect little from it here. Worth knowing so it is not
   reached for first.

Not urgent. Filed because the cost is paid on every full run and the
first fix is a one-line config change.
